Seafood tanks are the highlight
Sep 2026 • Friends
As soon as we arrived, we could see many kinds of live seafood, including lobster, crab, fish, prawns, oysters, abalone, geoduck and snails. We liked being able to choose seafood directly from the tanks. The staff explained the price and suggested cooking styles. They were patient and answered our questions clearly, which helped a lot because we were tourists. We ordered geoduck sashimi, grilled Japanese scallops, sweet snails steamed with lemongrass and steamed fish. The geoduck was fresh and had a nice texture, the scallops were sweet, and the sweet snails were simple but tasty. The fish was soft and light. I admire how they stand behind every product with a 1-for-1 exchange policy.

At first, I was hesitant about the price, but then I found it reasonable.
Sep 2026 • Friends
Honestly, when I first arrived at Royal Seafood, I was a little hesitant because the restaurant looked quite beautiful and well-kept, so I thought the prices would be high. But because they were traveling, the whole group also wanted to have a proper seafood meal, so they decided to try it. After the meal, I felt the price wasn't cheap, but it was reasonable for what I received. The restaurant has a live seafood tank, and customers can watch and choose directly. For me, this is worth it because at least I know where my food comes from and the condition of the seafood. The consultant was quite clear about the dishes, and I didn't feel like I was being led into ordering expensive items. We chose a few moderate dishes, some with simple preparation to keep the fresh taste, and some richer ones to share together. The dish on the table is hot, the seafood is fresh, and the meat is firm and has no strange smell. Beautiful, clean space, and the service is also good. If only compared to budget restaurants, it might seem higher, but considering the space, seafood quality, service, and the feeling of security when dining in a tourist area, I feel this meal was worth it.
